claim.why_it_matters: 15.73.3 rule 1 gives the normative arithmetic expression that native-arithmetic FUNCTION PI approximates. The PDF prints the fractional part as one unbroken 31-digit run; the markdown injects a space before the final two digits ('...327 95'). No digit is lost or altered, but any reader or tool copying the constant can truncate at the space and silently obtain 0.14159265358979323846264338327 - wrong from the 30th decimal onward.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent pixel measurement rather than by re-reading OCR text. Re-rendered specs page 933 (ISO printed page 903, 15.73 PI function) at 300 dpi to a clean directory (E:/Temp/specrecon/v933b/spec_p933.png, 2550x3300) and profiled column ink over both constant lines.

RULE 1 (y 1360-1440): the only interior blank gaps >= 12 px are at x=590 (17 px) and x=626 (15 px), which are the two genuine spaces flanking the '+' in '(3 + 0.'. Every gap inside the fractional digit run measures 3-7 px, i.e. ordinary inter-glyph advance. Connected ink runs on the line = 37, exactly '(' + '3' + '+' + '0' + '.' + 31 digits + ')'. So the PDF prints one unbroken 31-digit run and the claim quotes the PDF correctly. Visual check of a 6x magnified crop of the tail agrees: '...2384626433832795)' with even digit spacing and no break before '95'.

RULE 3 (y 1840-1920): no interior gap exceeds 8 px anywhere on the line outside the left margin - there is not even a '+' to supply a real space for comparison. Connected ink runs = 36, exactly '3' + '.' + 33 digits + '.'. The PDF prints an unbroken '3.141592653589793238462643383279503.'.

Calibration point that makes this decisive: on this page a genuine printed word-space is 15-17 px, while the widest gap inside either digit run is 8 px. A printed space is therefore excluded, not merely unobserved.

MARKDOWN: the extra character is really in the committed transcription, not an artifact of the page-slicing tool. Grepped specs/ISO_COBOL.md directly and dumped raw codepoints: line 37348 is '(3 + 0.14159265358979323846264338327 95)' and line 37356 is '3.14159265358979323846264338327 9503.', with U+0020 (0x20) at the break in both.

BENIGN EXPLANATIONS RULED OUT: not line wrapping or reflow - each markdown line is roughly 38-40 characters, so the space sits mid-token nowhere near any wrap measure; not hyphenation - no hyphen is present or implied; not page-break furniture - both lines are mid-page body text; not a misquote - both sources are quoted exactly as they read.

CONTENT IMPACT: digit fidelity is intact. De-spaced, rule 1 gives '1415926535897932384626433832795' = pi to 31 decimals (correctly unrounded, since decimal 32 of pi is 0), and rule 3 gives '141592653589793238462643383279503' = pi to 33 decimals correctly rounded up (decimals 32-34 of pi are 0,2,8, so ...79502|8 rounds to ...79503). Both match the PDF digit for digit. The corruption is confined to tokenization: each constant is no longer a single valid numeric literal. A whitespace-splitting extractor most likely yields two numbers; a reader truncating at the space obtains a value that diverges from pi at the 30th decimal, which is the failure mode the claim names.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, but the claim is under-scoped: the same defect occurs TWICE on this page, at the identical offset, and the claim reports only the first. Two spurious U+0020 characters are injected inside the normative numeric literals of 15.73.3 Returned value rules, each immediately after the 29th fractional digit:

  1. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:37348 - rule 1, native arithmetic (implementor-defined approximation)
     markdown: (3 + 0.14159265358979323846264338327 95)
     PDF:      (3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795)

  2. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:37356 - rule 3, standard-decimal arithmetic (the value the rule calls 'exactly')
     markdown: 3.14159265358979323846264338327 9503.
     PDF:      3.141592653589793238462643383279503.

Verified at 300 dpi by column-ink profiling: no gap inside either printed digit run exceeds 8 px, against 15-17 px for a real word-space on the same page, and connected-ink-run counts of 37 and 36 confirm 31 and 33 fractional digits respectively - matching the markdown's digit content exactly. No digit is lost or altered in either literal, so this is a transcription/tokenization defect, not a value error.

Fix: delete both U+0020 characters. Two refinements to the claim's framing. First, instance 2 is the more consequential and should carry the severity: rule 3 states the standard-decimal returned value is 'exactly' this constant, so it is a normative exact value admitting no tolerance, whereas rule 1 is explicitly an implementor-defined approximation - on that basis severity is better recorded as minor than cosmetic. Second, the repeated break at an identical digit offset in two independent literals is the signature of a fixed-width column split in the extraction pass, so the fix should sweep other long numeric literals in the transcription for the same artifact rather than patching these two lines in isolation.
